nodes.text: The After Party
Carrie is aglow. She's an absolute beauty. Charlie is gently touching her back.
They sit together on two stools so close together.
So what are you doing right here right now?
I really want to act, you know? I was in a couple high school productions. No big parts or nothing, but I loved it more than anything.
Now bring me full circle.
A guy was hitting on me at work, asked me out. I don't know anyone yet, so I figured why not. Now here I am.
All tired lonesome lonely, and more than a little drunk.
How far do you have to drive?
Thirty minutes.
My place is within five walking. You're welcome to crash on my couch.
Why thank you Charlie, how very nice of you to offer.
Charlie's Apartment
Charlie and Caroline are making out on the couch. Kissing lightly, tenderly.
How very nice indeed.
I'm really very tired you know.
You're welcome to join me in bed.
It's okay. The couch is fine.
There's not room enough for us both on the couch.
Yeah, I'm really tired Charlie.
Cool. Cool.
Charlie pulls back and stands up. She settles into the couch. He puts a blanket on her.
Good dreams Caroline.
She's either asleep or unresponsive. Her face is blank, but sweet.
I'm just standing here and watching her sleep. I think I'll continue doing this. I should probably talk about something, to fill the void of me just staring and remembering her touch, her taste.
She got to me good, no, more grand than good, something about her, just her way of being, her style and her eyes, learning all about me. I can't take my eyes off her. I can't stop thinking about her.
Charlie sits in a chair across from her.
The blanket rises and falls. The room holds very still.
Time passes. He's fallen asleep. His hair wildly fluctuates, though he stays still.
It's like a force of nature is messing up his hair despite him staying stationary.
It is morning now, the blanket is still on the couch, but Carrie is gone.
